newsitem.title: NORWAY: ALPINE SKIING-KJUS WINS RACE, ALPHAND TAKES TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-KJUS WINS RACE, ALPHAND TAKES TITLE.

text.p: Norway's Lasse Kjus, denied victory in a World Cup downhill on Saturday when high winds forced officials to rule the race invalid, won Sunday's re-run.
The 26-year-old Norwegian stormed down the icy 2,641-metre Olympiabakken course in one minute 27.12 seconds.
Italy's Pietro Vitalini was second in 1:27.26 while Canada's Edi Podivinsky, third in Saturday's aborted race, returned to the podium with a time of 1:27.56.

Luc Alphand, who complained bitterly about being forced to race in what he considered dangerous conditions on Saturday, finished fifth. The result was enough to give the Frenchman his third consecutive downhill title.
After the race Alphand immediately turned his attention to a super-G race scheduled for later on Sunday.
